identity.name: Federal Republic of Central America
native_names: Provincias Unidas del Centro de America

land.text: Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica: the Central American provinces 'between the 8th and 18th parallel north'

predecessors.note: The provinces joined the Mexican Empire on 5 January 1822 and left it on 1 July 1823, 'except for the state of Chiapas'.

land.text: Guatemala, whose president Rafael Carrera issued the decree of 17 April 1839 dissolving the federation

successors.note: Los Altos (Quetzaltenango) was a sixth state of the federation in 1838-1839 and sits inside this land; Cliopatria has it as Los Altos 1840-1841.

land.text: El Salvador, which 'declared independence from the Federal Republic of Central America' on 30 January 1841

successors.note: El Salvador kept the federal flag until 1841; Cliopatria's row begins 1840.

land.text: Costa Rica, seceded 15 November 1838 (and from 1 April 1829 to February 1831)

capitals.name: Sonsonate
capitals.note: The capital 'moved ... to the Salvadoran city of Sonsonate on 5 February 1834'.

capitals.name: San Salvador
capitals.note: 'San Salvador became the federal capital in June 1834.'

correction.text: the five Central American states, drawn as in the 1824 shape, from 1 July 1823

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1824 but the page dates the federation to the declaration of independence from Mexico on 1 July 1823. The 1823 shape is the 1824 shape (the First Mexican Empire dossier carries Central America in its own shape until July 1823).

444k km2 against the infobox 'approximately 200,000 square miles (520,000 km2)' (undated; ratio 0.85). The shape holds Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica, 7 percent of Belize and 11 percent of Chiapas (the Soconusco). The page says coastal Belize was 'occupied by the British' and the Mosquito Coast was claimed but not held, so the small Belize share is an overreach of a few cells; the Soconusco was 'claimed by Central America and Mexico over which neither had full control' (federation page) and 'the lowlands, including the Soconusco, preferred Central America' (Soconusco page), so it stays in. Costa Rica's secession of 1 April 1829 to February 1831 is in the ledger and not drawn by Cliopatria.
443,260 km2: the same land with the capital at Sonsonate and then San Salvador. No territorial change from 1833.

The Cliopatria shape (all five states) holds for 1836-1837 only; Nicaragua left on 30 April 1838, Honduras on 26 October and Costa Rica on 15 November 1838, and Carrera's decree dissolved the republic on 17 April 1839. Years 1838-1839 are in the new keyframe.

correction.text: Guatemala and El Salvador, the states still in the federation after the three secessions of 1838

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1838-1839: the federation reduced to Guatemala and El Salvador after the three secessions of 1838 ('Nicaragua seceded ... on 30 April 1838', 'Honduras did the same on 26 October', Costa Rica 'on 15 November'). The page also says the federal government 'considered separating Los Altos from Guatemala' in 1838-1839; the cells stay inside Guatemala here.

region.text: Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica: the Central American provinces 'between the 8th and 18th parallel north'

ledger.note: 1823: Central America declares independence from Mexico. 'After Iturbide abdicated on 19 March 1823, the congress declared independence from Mexico on 1 July 1823', 'except for the state of Chiapas'. It followed the Act of Independence of 15 September 1821 and annexation to the Mexican Empire on 5 January 1822.

1824: the constitution makes the Federal Republic of Central America. 'On 22 November, the constitution was formally adopted after all 64 members of the assembly signed it' (five states; a Federal District from 1835). The page does not describe a change of name; Cliopatria's name for the row is United Provinces of Central America.
1829: Costa Rica secedes. 'On 1 April 1829, Costa Rica seceded from the Federal Republic of Central America'; it 'rejoined in February 1831'. Cliopatria keeps it inside the shape.
1831: Costa Rica rejoins the federation in February.
1834: the federal capital moves from Guatemala City to Sonsonate on 5 February and to San Salvador in June.
1838: Nicaragua secedes. 'Nicaragua seceded from the Federal Republic of Central America on 30 April 1838.'
1838: Honduras secedes. 'Honduras did the same on 26 October.'
1838: Costa Rica secedes for the second time on 15 November.

region.text: Guatemala and El Salvador, the states still in the federation after the three secessions of 1838

ledger.note: 1839: Carrera dissolves the federation. 'On 17 April, Guatemalan President Rafael Carrera issued a decree dissolving the Federal Republic of Central America'; Congress accepted it on 14 July 1839; El Salvador declared independence on 30 January 1841. The second civil war ran 1838-1840.

wars.name: Central American civil war of 1827-1829
wars.outcome: Morazan's forces took Guatemala City: 'The city surrendered on 12 April and Morazan's soldiers entered it the following day, ending the civil war.'
wars.note: The page dates the war 'From 1827 to 1829' beginning with Prado's invasion in early 1827. No territory changed hands.

wars.name: Central American civil war of 1838-1840
wars.outcome: The states declared independence one by one (Nicaragua, Honduras, Costa Rica in 1838; Guatemala by Carrera's decree of 17 April 1839; El Salvador in 1841).
wars.note: 'The republic descended into a second civil war from 1838 to 1840.' The page does not say who ended it.

certainty.note: The page gives the area but no boundary: the Belize coast was British-held, the Mosquito Coast was claimed but not held, and the Soconusco was claimed by Mexico (formal claim 1825) and Guatemala. The line between the five states is administrative.

sources.title: Federal Republic of Central America
sources.note: Identity, dates (1 July 1823, 22 November 1824, 17 April 1839), capitals, area (520,000 km2), presidents, secessions of Costa Rica and Nicaragua and Honduras, civil wars, claims over Belize and the Mosquito Coast.

sources.title: Soconusco
sources.note: Soconusco's status: Chiapas annexed by Mexico in 1824, the Soconusco lowlands preferred Central America, Mexico's claim of 1825, Guatemala's 1840 claim, Mexican troops in 1842, the 1882 treaty.

notes: Cliopatria's row is 1824-1839; the dossier starts on 1 July 1823 (the page) and adds a 1823 keyframe, and adds a 1838-1839 keyframe for the three secessions (the 1836 shape keeps all five states to 1839). The Soconusco (11 percent of Chiapas in the shape) is drawn inside the federation although Mexico claimed it from 1825 and took it in 1842, after the federation's end; the federated-republic-of-mexico dossier leaves it out. Costa Rica's secession of 1829-1831 is recorded as a loss and a gain although Cliopatria's Costa Rica row begins in 1840 (counterpart republic-of-costa-rica); El Salvador remained in the federation until 30 January 1841 and has no loss event here (the dossier ends in April 1839; the El Salvador group should carry 1839-1841). Los Altos (1838-1839 as a sixth state) is not dated by the page. Guanacaste/Nicoya joining Costa Rica in 1824 is not on either page. The page names the republic 'Federal Republic of Central America'; the infobox gives 22 November 1824 for the constitution. Page budget: two pages.
